chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: Lips's band, Cincinnati and Fletcher Henderson
summary: Lips had a great band after Artie Shaw; in Cincinnati Ramirez met Linton Garner and Fletcher Henderson, and Chubby Jackson helped Pettiford come to New York.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: How big a band did Lips have then?
He had a band that was the greatest, I'm telling you. He had just left Artie Shaw, do you remember? He had arrangements... Do you remember that record he made with Artie Shaw...?
How long were you with him, do you think?
Well, I don't know. Not quite a year. Because we were able to... We traveled to Cincinnati. That's where I met Erroll's brother, who was playing piano for Fletcher Henderson and writing.

Linton Garner, that's right. We played the Cotton Club in Cincinnati, you know, and they were playing in Covington across the river. So I spoke to Fletcher, and I said, "Fletcher, it's the first time I've been here; this city looks very worn down." He said, "Yes, I call it Cinci-Nasty." [LAUGHS] He was staying with a girl named Muriel or somebody.

He was conducting and playing when he got through -- but he was mostly conducting. He also was in the Happy Hour or something, a club in Minneapolis. And that's where we picked up Oscar Pettiford. Chubby Jackson was the bass player in the band, and he liked Oscar... He was really the one that was responsible for Oscar coming to New York -- Chubby Jackson.
